CBS News' Aidan Stretch is on the ground in Ceuta, Spain, where an estimated 60,000 migrants crossed the border from Morocco this week. The rush of migrants turned deadly, with some drowning as they tried to swim to reach the territory. Stretch spoke to several migrants, many of whom were planning on going back over the border after not being able to find food. Spain's Ministry of the Interior said more than 25,000 migrants who arrived at the border have been sent back to Morocco and that more than 150 migrants are being removed from Ceuta per minute. #spain #immigration #morocco #immigrant #ceuta

videos.caption: Thousands of migrants from Morocco poured over the country's border with Spain and into the country’s African enclave of Ceuta after swimming around border barriers to reach the territory. The latest wave comes after more than 1,500 migrants arrived in Ceuta by sea over the past week, according to regional authorities. Ceuta's leader is now urging Spain's national government to declare an emergency as the enclave faces another major surge at the European Union's only land border with Africa. This border breach comes at the same time as President Trump sounds the alarm about the rising number of migrants coming from Africa and other parts of the world who he says are “invading” European countries.

Make sure you do not go to the Agafay desert… you need to make sure you go to the further desert because it is absolutely gorgeous   I do think that I explain in my video, however, it goes a little bit deeper than just a city having small streets and being uncomfortable, because of the way that men act I think it is directly tied tourism , so while I would not say avoid Marrakesh, I would just say, be vigilant and ignore, and that speak to you if you’re alone. The bottom line is travel to Morocco is safe. Tourism and Morocco is safe. Moroccans are very kind in hospital people, so should you travel to Morocco? Yes. Morocco is safe for solo female travelers.
